## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: rules of the road, part one
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The whole manual carries an old content-currency date (stated in part A), so any rule here may have changed since; the freshness debt in part A covers every fact in this section.
The stop-sign position conflicts on one page: the quoted law says that with no stop line or crosswalk you stop where you can see cross traffic before entering, while a later bullet says to stop with your front even with the sign; only the law's wording is taught (verify TN-ROAD1-D-STOPPOINT) [A05].
The stopping-distance chart extracted as scattered numbers, so only the manual's worked deer example and the National Safety Council figure are taught; the example's time and distance values do not match the chart exactly and are taught only as the manual's illustration [A05].
Crash statistics for intersections and work zones are figures the manual quotes for past years and are taught as attributed to the manual, not refreshed here [A08].
The Basic Speed Rule is described by the manual as a principle rather than a statute and is taught that way.

corpus_stability.reason: The Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual says its content is current as of July 1, 2022 and its back cover carries one March 2025 print authorization; nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year, but the content date is old, so freshness is held as debt rather than assumed.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page 63 quotes Tennessee law that with no stop line or crosswalk a driver stops at the point nearest the cross road with a view of traffic, then says that with no pavement markings the front of the car should be even with the stop sign; confirm which position the test expects.
